scope: Fresh console/PC-to-Android and mobile-adjacent projects found by GitHub/web search and qualified against maintainer source. Every status distinguishes released APKs, local-build-only targets, device reports, and incomplete work. No live catalog or tracked files were changed.

projects.title: Burnout 3: Takedown Original Xbox Android Static Recompilation (b3x)
projects.game: Burnout 3: Takedown (Original Xbox, North American NTSC-U retail release)
projects.platform: Original Xbox NTSC-U XBE → Android 11+ ARM64 (arm64-v8a), Vulkan 1.1+; Windows and Linux desktop builds are also documented
projects.status: The maintainer labels the Android build 1.0.0 and reports races at 55–60 fps on an Android 13 Infinix X6815D (Dimensity 920/Mali-G68) and 36–44 fps on an Android 15 POCO M3 (Snapdragon 662/Adreno 610). These are project-reported tests. The README gives local build/install instructions; the GitHub Releases API showed no published release assets when checked on 2026-10-16. The game is not included.
projects.summary: An Android-specific static recompilation of Burnout 3’s original Xbox NTSC-U executable: xboxrecomp lifts the XBE instructions to C, which is compiled for ARM64; a native Vulkan renderer translates NV2A graphics work, and SDL2 supplies Android app, audio, touch, and controller integration. The README credits sp00nznet’s Burnout 3 recompilation and xboxrecomp toolkit. A user-owned ISO or extracted game directory is required; no game data is shipped.
projects.strategy: Static Original Xbox x86-to-C recompilation with an Android ARM64 build and native Vulkan renderer; SDL2 Android app shell and user-supplied NTSC-U game data.
projects.language: English (the supported NTSC-U game image documented by the project)
projects.source_available: Public source repository; GitHub identifies MIT. The README credits sp00nznet/Burnout 3 recompilation and its MIT xboxrecomp toolkit. No retail game data is included; a user-owned Original Xbox NTSC-U copy is required. No GitHub release asset was present at the 2026-10-16 check.
projects.subtype: Original Xbox static recompilation; Android Vulkan port

projects.title: Yoshi’s Island: Super Mario Advance 3 Android Static Recompilation
projects.game: Yoshi’s Island: Super Mario Advance 3 (USA, Game Boy Advance)
projects.platform: Game Boy Advance USA → Android 9+ ARM64 (API 28+); Linux is used for host validation and build preparation
projects.status: Experimental v0.9 ARM64 APK is available in the GitHub release tagged “Descarga” (2026-10-04; 31.8 MB). The README still says the 0.9 upload is pending, so its download note is stale. The maintainer reports 120 fps on a Pixel 7 Pro with v0.8; this is not independently measured and does not validate v0.9’s touch-layout editor. The README says full-game/level coverage, audio, saves, lifecycle and physical controller checks remain incomplete.
projects.summary: A game-specific GBA static recompilation using the GBARecomp toolchain and project-specific address/disassembly metadata. Game and BIOS code are translated to C++ and compiled for ARM64 with strict native dispatch and no interpreter fallback. The Android app supports on-screen controls, configurable layouts, and partial English, Latin American Spanish, and Brazilian Portuguese text. Users provide their own matching USA ROM and GBA BIOS; neither is included.
projects.strategy: Strict static recompilation of GBA program code to C++, compiled for Android ARM64 using GBARecomp and project-specific disassembly/address tables; unsupported calls do not fall back to an interpreter.
projects.language: English, Latin American Spanish, and Brazilian Portuguese partial menu/name text; the README says graphics labels, credits, and Mario Bros remain English.
projects.source_available: Public source repository, but no repository-wide license grant was found. The README reports that the GBARecomp engine uses PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 and arm-recomp-core uses MIT; those terms do not grant rights to the game or BIOS. The user supplies a matching USA ROM and GBA BIOS; generated game code and the ROM are not included.
projects.subtype: Nintendo Game Boy Advance static recompilation for Android

projects.title: WWF WrestleMania: The Arcade Game Recompilation for Android TV
projects.game: WWF WrestleMania: The Arcade Game (Arcade, Wolf Unit REV 1.30)
projects.platform: Midway Wolf Unit arcade (TMS34010, REV 1.30) → desktop Windows/macOS/Linux and Android TV; NVIDIA Shield TV Pro is the only documented Android device, with no phone/tablet test claimed
projects.status: The recompiled game boots, passes its power-up self-test, runs attract mode, and plays matches using original art; fidelity checks against arcade hardware remain listed as next. The README and Android-specific notes report the Android TV app built and run on an NVIDIA Shield TV Pro, while also identifying some Android packaging/data-copy steps as untested; no Android release is listed and other devices have not been tried.
projects.summary: A C recompilation of the original TMS34010 game program translated from the historical assembly/disassembly source, hosted with SDL2 and a Wolf Unit hardware runtime. It supports desktop systems and an Android TV app with controller navigation. Users provide the original game images and sound ROM data; these are not included. The project separates optional display/gameplay modifications from the original behavior.
projects.strategy: Static TMS34010-to-C recompilation with a Wolf Unit runtime and SDL2 platform layer; Android TV uses an SDL2 activity and controller input.
projects.source_available: Public GPL-3.0 source. Original arcade image and sound data are not distributed; the user must supply the source game data. The README links the historical assembly/disassembly source and documents the project’s license.
projects.subtype: Arcade TMS34010 static recompilation; Android TV port

projects.title: The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Clean-Room Engine for Android
projects.platform: Windows PC/Steam 32-bit x86 → Android ARM64 (primary target) and Linux x86-64
projects.status: The v0.1.0 release (2026-10-12) is explicitly an early scaffold, not a playable game: the repository reports 0 of 655 native function bodies implemented and nothing rendered. It does contain a recovered/registered API surface, engine lifecycle scaffolding, reproducible binding-table extraction from the user’s own install, and CI cross-compilation for Android ARM64.
projects.summary: An independent MIT-licensed C++17 clean-room engine reimplementation targeting the Windows/Steam PC game’s runtime behavior on Android ARM64 and Linux. It reads a user-owned Steam installation at runtime and ships no game code, data, sprites, audio, video, or text. The first release registers 655 Lua-facing method names and includes Android cross-build checks, but implements no native method bodies or renderer yet.
projects.strategy: Clean-room C++17 engine/API reimplementation from a compatibility specification and user-local binding-table analysis; it does not statically translate the game executable.
projects.source_available: Public MIT source. The README describes the implementation as clean-room and says it contains no game code/assets/data; it reads files from a user-owned Steam install. The project does not grant rights to the commercial game.
projects.subtype: Early-stage clean-room engine reimplementation with Android ARM64 target

projects.title: Bully: Anniversary Edition Android-to-Switch Homebrew Port
projects.platform: Android arm64-v8a app v1.4.311 → Nintendo Switch Horizon OS (AArch64 homebrew)
projects.status: Work in progress: the maintainer says the Switch wrapper boots and runs the game, but it is unfinished and still uses temporary workarounds. Installation requires the matching user-owned Android APK data and native libraries; the repository distributes neither.
projects.summary: A game-specific Nintendo Switch homebrew wrapper for the Android release of Bully: Anniversary Edition. It loads the original Android ARM64 game library and adapts the required runtime calls through a Switch-side compatibility layer; it does not decompile or reimplement the game. The project is derived from fgsfds’ max_nx Switch loader and the Bully Vita port lineage.
projects.strategy: Android ARM64 native-binary compatibility port: retain the original game .so and bridge the Android runtime/API surface to Nintendo Switch Horizon OS via a Switch homebrew loader and shims.
projects.source_available: Public MIT-licensed wrapper source. No Android APK, game libraries, or game assets are included; the user must supply files from an officially obtained v1.4.311 copy. The repository is a derivative of fgsfds/max_nx; upstream/game terms remain separate.

projects.title: Streets of Rage X Android-to-Switch Homebrew Port
projects.game: Streets of Rage X (OpenBOR fan game; Android release)
projects.platform: Android arm64-v8a release → Nintendo Switch Horizon OS (AArch64 homebrew)
projects.status: Release 1.0.1 (2026-08-14) is published. The maintainer documents that the port can play all stages after the initial asset extraction, while videos are stubbed and first-run loading can be slow. It requires the user to provide the Android libraries and game package from the Android release.
projects.summary: A MIT-licensed Nintendo Switch homebrew loader for the Android release of the OpenBOR fan game Streets of Rage X. It loads the Android ARM64 SDL2/OpenBOR libraries and bridges Android-facing JNI, libc, EGL/GLES, audio, and lifecycle calls to Switch services; it is not a source recompilation or Android emulator. The project does not bundle the Android game package or its assets.
projects.strategy: Android ABI/API compatibility layer on Switch: execute the provided Android ARM64 libraries while bridging fake JNI, bionic-to-newlib libc, EGL/GLES imports, audio, and SDL activity lifecycle to native Switch homebrew services.
projects.language: English (the project wrapper; game language follows the user-supplied Android game release)
projects.source_available: Public MIT-licensed Switch wrapper source. Users supply the Android binaries and OpenBOR package from the separately distributed fan game; the port repository says it does not include the game assets.
projects.subtype: Android OpenBOR game-to-Switch API translation/homebrew port

projects.title: Viridite Android-to-Horizon Compatibility Layer
projects.platform: Android ARM64/ARM32 native NDK applications → Nintendo Switch Horizon OS (AArch64)
projects.status: Experimental source-available compatibility layer. The maintainer reports Hill Climb Racing playable on real Switch hardware with touch input, audio, and a locked 60 fps; the README still notes a crash in the Shop screen and that full save-persistence round-trip testing is outstanding. The README says other detected games are not thereby confirmed playable.
projects.summary: A Nintendo Switch homebrew launcher and Android-runtime compatibility/translation layer. It runs Android native libraries on Horizon OS without Android or a whole-device emulator, adapting the needed Android ABI/API, JNI, filesystem, graphics, and audio behavior to Switch-side services. Hill Climb Racing 1.x is the hardware-tested target; this is a reusable software framework, not a catalog entry for each recognized APK.
projects.strategy: Runtime Android ABI/API translation for Horizon OS: load Android native ELF libraries and bridge JNI, libc, graphics, storage, and audio behavior to Nintendo Switch services.
projects.source_available: Public source repository under a custom source-available, non-commercial, attribution/share-alike license; it is not a standard permissive open-source license. No third-party Android application binaries or game data are included.
projects.subtype: Android application compatibility layer for Nintendo Switch homebrew
